title: Prevent operator from pruning user-managed Secrets during on-prem Helm upgrades
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Multiple on-prem customers reported that after applying the operator Helm chart upgrade, several customer-managed Kubernetes Secrets used by tenant workloads were unexpectedly deleted. This caused downstream tenant services (model-serving sidecars and ingress auth) to fail until secrets were restored from backups. Initial triage shows operator's post-upgrade pruning step is overly aggressive when Helm hooks change and when annotation keys are migrated between releases. We need a hotfix that prevents pruning of Secrets unless they are explicitly owned by the operator.

Impact: Affected customers experienced degraded availability (15-60 minutes remediation) for a subset of tenants. This is a P0 customer escalation for Dedicated/Private on-prem clusters with strict namespace separation.

Goals: 1) Ship a 2.9.1 hotfix that introduces a conservative prune whitelist and safe-guard annotations. 2) Publish rollback/runbook and communicate to impacted customers. 3) Add CI/integration tests to catch similar regressions in future upgrades.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Khan: Customer support escalated incident for two on-prem customers (CUST-437, CUST-502). Both reported missing secrets after operator Helm upgrade. Opening ticket and assigning to Marco for investigation.

2026-03-10 11:40 - Marco Rivera: Reproduced in staging by performing chart upgrade from 2.8.4 -> 2.9.0 with sample tenant. Observed operator post-upgrade reconciliation invoked pruner controller which removed Secrets with annotation key migration (old key redwood.io/managed=true -> new key redwood.io/owner=operator). Root cause hypothesis: prune predicate uses presence of annotation key rather than explicit ownership label.

2026-03-10 14:05 - Marco Rivera: Immediate mitigation: disable automatic prune in Helm upgrade notes and recommend customers set manual pause annotation (redwood.io/upgrade-pause=true) before upgrade. Sent stovepipe comms to affected accounts with remediation steps and backup restore instructions.

2026-03-11 08:33 - SRE (Li Chen): Collected controller logs and archived to incident dashboard: https://redwood-internal/dashboards/incident/ENG-256789. Added correlating helm history and k8s events. Noted operator reconciler logged deletion reason: 'ownerRef/annotation mismatch during prune'.

2026-03-12 16:10 - Marco Rivera: Implemented patch to prune controller: prune only Secrets where label redwood.io/owned=true AND metadata.ownerReferences includes operator CR, OR Secret has explicit annotation redwood.io/prunable=true. Added migration helper that maps legacy annotation keys to new keys without triggering prune. Unit tests added. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/6142

2026-03-13 09:00 - Design (Priya Das): Reviewed user communication templates. Suggested adding explicit rollback/restore checklist and ephemeral namespace test before upgrade. Approved PR for customer-facing messaging.

2026-03-14 13:20 - Security (Daniel Park): Quick review – change does not introduce elevated privileges. Recommended adding e2e test that runs with restricted RBAC roles. Marking security_review_required=false for now.

2026-03-15 07:45 - Marco Rivera: QA notes: Integration tests passed in CI against KinD and a staged on-prem cluster. Ran staged upgrade on canary tenant in staging and observed no secret deletions. Preparing hotfix release notes and rollout plan.

2026-03-15 10:02 - Customer Success (Hannah White): Drafted customer comms for CUST-437 and CUST-502 with scheduled maintenance window option. Prepared runbook link for customers who already hit the issue.
acceptance_criteria: hotfix operator-2.9.1 built and deployed to staging cluster
integration tests covering legacy annotation migration and pruning logic added to CI
runbook published with explicit restore steps and Helm pre-upgrade pause instructions
customer-facing email templates approved and sent to impacted customers
monitoring alert added for unexpected Secret deletions during upgrades
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR #6142 to release branch after 2-approver review and green CI
2) Cut operator-2.9.1-hotfix image and publish helm chart with prune disabled by default
3) Deploy to internal staging and run full upgrade scenario against canary tenant
4) After 1h stable, schedule gradual rollout to affected customers during maintenance windows (CS to coordinate), enabling verbose reconcile logging
5) Monitor secret-deletion alert and rollback immediately if triggered (helm rollback to 2.9.0)
